jobs.location: Dallas, Texas, United States; Houston, Texas, United States
jobs.description:
Job Purpose:

BTIG seeks a highly motivated and high‑performing Investment Banking Analyst to join the Energy &Infrastructure team based in Texas (Dallas or Houston). The Analyst will play a critical role in supporting senior bankers across a variety of domestic and international corporate finance transactions. These include sell-side and buy-side mergers and acquisitions (M&A), public and private equity and debt capital raises, and strategic advisory assignments.

The ideal candidate will possess a strong financial background, exceptional analytical skills, and a keen interest in the broader energy and infrastructure landscape, including the upstream, midstream, downstream, and oilfield services (OFS) sub-sectors.

Duties & Responsibilities:

- Build, maintain, and analyze complex financial models, including discounted cash flow (DCF), net asset value (NAV) for E&P companies, leveraged buyouts (LBO), accretion/dilution, and comparable company/precedent transaction analyses.

- Assist in the day-to-day execution of M&A and capital markets transactions, coordinating closely with internal teams, legal counsel, and clients.

- Prepare comprehensive marketing materials, including pitch books, confidential information memoranda (CIMs), management presentations, and board materials.

- Conduct in-depth research and strategic analysis on domestic and international energy markets. Monitor commodity price trends, regulatory changes, macro-economic drivers, and competitive landscapes across various sub-sectors.

- Manage data rooms and coordinate the due diligence process for active transactions, including the detailed review of technical and financial documents.

- Communicate effectively with senior bankers, clients, lawyers, accountants, and other advisors. Participate in client meetings and calls, providing analytical support and taking detailed notes for strategic follow-ups.

Requirements & Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business, Engineering, or a related quantitative discipline with a strong academic track record.

- 1–2 years of experience in Investment Banking, M&A, Corporate Development, Private Equity, or a closely related transaction advisory field. Prior exposure to the Energy, Infrastructure, or Oil & Gas sectors is highly preferred.

- Strong understanding of corporate finance and M&A processes. Familiarity with oil and gas specific valuation metrics (e.g., EV/EBITDAX, $/flowing barrel, reserve life, NAV) is a strong plus.

- Exceptional proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint. Experience with financial data platforms (e.g., Bloomberg, FactSet, CapIQ) and industry-specific tools (e.g., Enverus) is advantageous.

- Outstanding analytical and problem-solving abilities with high attention to detail. Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

- Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a lean deal team structure. Must be able to manage multiple workstreams and projects simultaneously under tight deadlines in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment.

- SIE, Series 79, and Series 63 licenses are preferred, or the candidate must have the ability to obtain them shortly after joining.

jobs.title: Investment Banking, Capital Markets Operations, Account Onboarding (Associate/Vice President)
jobs.location: New York, New York, United States; San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.description:
Job Purpose:

BTIG is seeking a Capital Markets Operations Associate / Vice President focused on account onboarding and account lifecycle management. This role is responsible for end-to-end onboarding and opening of DVP (Delivery versus Payment) and Cash-Custody accounts across multiple clearing firms, ongoing account maintenance, and broader administrative workflows that support Capital Markets coverage and governance.

The position requires strong operational execution, attention to detail, and the ability to coordinate across internal stakeholders (Sales, Trading, Syndicate, Capital Markets, Legal, Compliance, Risk, Finance, Technology) and external clearing firms to ensure accounts are opened and maintained accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with firm policies and applicable regulatory requirements.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Account Onboarding & Account Opening (DVP / Cash-Custody; Multi-Clearing Firm)

- Manage end-to-end onboarding for institutional and corporate clients from intake through account activation and post-opening validation.

- Open and establish  DVP  and  Cash-Custody  accounts across  multiple clearing firms , including coordinating requirements, forms, and clearing firm-specific processes.

- Own the NIGO resolution process: identify documentation gaps, communicate requirements to stakeholders, and drive timely completion.

- Validate and ensure accuracy of account data and setup parameters (e.g., legal entity name, tax status, addresses, authorized contacts/signers, and settlement instructions/SSIs).

- Maintain clear onboarding documentation, checklists, and audit-ready records aligned with internal policy and control expectations.

Account Maintenance / Client Account Services

- Perform ongoing account maintenance, including:

- Refreshing documentation  (periodic and event-driven updates)

- Name and address changes  and related data updates

- Updates to authorized contacts/signatories, account attributes, and settlement details as needed

- Ensure all maintenance requests are properly approved, documented, and updated across internal systems and clearing firm platforms, as applicable.

- Serve as a point of escalation for time-sensitive account issues impacting trading, settlement, or client experience.

Month-End Statement Delivery & Delivery Preference Requests

- Manage  month-end statement delivery requests , including changes to recipients, delivery method, and statement access troubleshooting.

- Coordinate with clearing firms and internal teams to ensure accurate and timely statement delivery and issue resolution.

Corporate Account-Related Operational Support (ATM Programs / Buybacks / Legal & Compliance Requests)

- Coordinate and track corporate account-related items, partnering closely with Legal and Compliance on request intake, documentation, and execution readiness.

- Support operational requirements connected to  ATMs (at-the-market programs)  and  issuer buybacks , including account setup readiness, process coordination, and recordkeeping in line with internal policy and required approvals.

Administrative Responsibilities / Governance (Including CRM Coverage Approvals)

- Manage broader administrative and control processes supporting account governance, including the  CRM account coverage approval process :

- Intake and validation of coverage requests

- Routing for approvals consistent with firm policy

- Documenting outcomes and ensuring accurate CRM updates

- Support periodic reviews, data quality initiatives, and operational documentation/procedures tied to account lifecycle governance.

Controls, Risk Management & Process Improvement

- Ensure adherence to firm policies, clearing firm requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.

- Identify operational risks (e.g., inaccurate SSIs, incomplete documentation, unauthorized changes, statement delivery errors) and escalate appropriately.

- Track and report onboarding volumes, cycle times, NIGO trends, and service performance; recommend improvements to reduce friction and improve controls.

- (VP-level) Drive enhancements to onboarding/maintenance workflows, standardization across clearing firms, and training/mentoring of junior team members.

Requirements & Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience.

- Experience in capital markets operations, client onboarding/new accounts, account services, or clearing firm/custody-related operational roles.

- Strong attention to detail with a demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent, time-sensitive workflows.

- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including comfort interacting with Legal, Compliance, Sales, Trading, and external clearing firm contacts.

- High level of ownership, sound judgment, and a strong control mindset.

Preferred

- Hands-on experience opening and maintaining  DVP  and/or  Cash-Custody  accounts.

- Experience working across  multiple clearing firms  and navigating clearing firm onboarding portals/processes.

- Familiarity supporting operational workflows tied to corporate programs (e.g., ATMs and issuer buybacks) in partnership with control functions.

- Strong Excel skills and comfort working across CRM and internal account master / workflow tools.

Core Competencies

- Client onboarding and documentation management

- Strong operational controls and audit-ready recordkeeping

- Ability to prioritize and execute under deadlines

- Cross-functional collaboration and escalation management

- Process improvement mindset and operational rigor

- Professional communication with internal and external stakeholders

jobs.title: Investment Banking, Capital Markets Operations, Securities Transfer & Settlement (Associate/Vice President)
jobs.location: New York, New York, United States; San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.description:
Job Purpose:

BTIG is seeking a Capital Markets Operations Associate / Vice President focused on securities transfers and transaction settlement in support of Capital Markets activity and trading. This role is responsible for the end-to-end management of transfer workflows—primarily  DWAC and DRS transfers —to ensure timely, accurate settlement of transactions across issuers, transfer agents, clearing firms, clients, and internal stakeholders.

The position requires deep familiarity with restricted securities processing, documentation standards, and close coordination with issuer and fund counsel to facilitate settlements. The role also supports critical “flow of funds” coordination for Capital Markets transactions, wire transfer authorization workflows for Venture Capital and Private Equity trading clients, and related clearing firm journals and settlement support.

Duties & Responsibilities:

DWAC / DRS Transfers – Primary Ownership

- Own the operational processing and oversight of  DWAC (Deposit/Withdrawal at Custodian)  and  DRS (Direct Registration System)  transfers for  all Capital Markets transactions and trading-related settlement .

- Manage transfer timelines and status tracking end-to-end; identify and resolve breaks and escalations to protect settlement dates.

- Coordinate transfer initiation, approvals, and delivery requirements across internal teams, clearing firms, and transfer agents.

Transfer Agent Relationship Management

- Serve as the primary point of contact for  transfer agents , maintaining strong working relationships to facilitate efficient processing.

- Manage service expectations and escalation paths with transfer agents; ensure consistent communication and accountability on aged items.

- Partner with internal stakeholders to standardize transfer workflows and documentation expectations by agent and security type.

Documentation Management for Securities Transfers & Restricted Stock

- Collect, review, and manage documentation required to process transfers and restricted securities, including (as applicable):

- Medallion Signature Guarantees

- Opinion letters

- Restricted stock / legend removal paperwork

- Corporate issuer instructions and supporting transfer documentation

- Ensure documentation packages are complete, accurate, and aligned with transfer agent and clearing firm requirements; drive resolution of NIGO items.

- Maintain organized, audit-ready records of transfer requests, approvals, and supporting materials.

Counsel Coordination (Issuer & Fund-Level) to Support Timely Settlement

- Liaise directly with  corporate issuer counsel  and  fund-level counsel  (VC/PE and other institutional clients) to ensure legal deliverables are coordinated and settlement timelines are met.

- Track open legal items impacting settlement (opinions, legends, representations, required forms) and drive to closure through proactive follow-up and escalation as needed.

Capital Markets “Flow of Funds” & Settlement Coordination

- Manage the  flow of funds process  for Capital Markets transactions, partnering with Operations and Finance to ensure appropriate cash movements, settlement readiness, and internal controls.

- Coordinate key settlement milestones and operational readiness across Capital Markets, Syndicate, Trading, Finance, and clearing firms.

Wire Transfer LOA Process (Venture Capital / Private Equity Trading Clients)

- Administer and control the  wire transfer LOA (Letter of Authorization) process  for VC and PE trading clients, including intake, validation, and routing per firm policy and required approvals.

- Ensure wire instructions are handled with strong controls and documentation discipline; coordinate with Finance/Operations for timely execution.

Clearing Firm Journals & Settlement Requests

- Process and track  journal requests  with BTIG’s clearing firms in support of settlement and client servicing needs.

- Investigate and resolve journal-related breaks, mismatches, or timing issues impacting settlement or client positions.

Ongoing Restricted Stock Settlement Management

- Own ongoing restricted stock settlement workflows, liaising with clients, clearing firms, and transfer agents to ensure timely delivery and receipt of securities.

- Monitor aged restricted settlements, proactively identify bottlenecks, and drive resolution to reduce settlement risk and improve client experience.

Affiliate Sales Support – Rule 144 and Broker Representation Letters

- Prepare and coordinate  Rule 144 filings  for affiliate sales, ensuring accurate collection of required information and timely submission support (consistent with firm process).

- Draft and manage  Broker Representation Letters  for affiliate and prospectus sales, coordinating with clients, counsel, and other stakeholders to complete execution and delivery requirements.

Controls, Risk Management & Process Improvement

- Maintain a strong control mindset across transfers, wires, and settlement activities, including documentation retention and escalation of exceptions.

- Identify operational risks (e.g., incorrect wire instructions, missing transfer documentation, delayed legal deliverables, settlement fails) and implement preventive controls and standardized workflows.

- Track volumes, cycle times, aged items, and recurring breaks; propose process enhancements to improve throughput and reduce risk.

- (VP-level) Mentor junior team members and lead improvements across transfer agent management, restricted stock processing, and settlement governance.

Requirements & Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience.

- Experience in securities operations with direct exposure to  settlement and/or securities transfers ; comfort managing time-sensitive, high-touch workflows.

- Strong understanding of DWAC/DRS concepts and the practical processing requirements across transfer agents and clearing firms (or demonstrated ability to learn quickly).

- Demonstrated ability to manage complex documentation requirements with excellent attention to detail.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to coordinate across clients, counsel, transfer agents, clearing firms, and internal stakeholders.

- High ownership, sound judgment, and a strong operational risk and controls mindset.

Preferred

- Prior experience managing  restricted stock  settlements and documentation (opinions, medallions, legend/restriction processing).

- Familiarity with  Rule 144  processing support and broker representation documentation workflows.

- Experience supporting Capital Markets transaction settlement and cash movement coordination (flow of funds).

- Proficiency with Excel and comfort working across internal workflow tools and clearing firm platforms.

Core Competencies

- Securities transfer and settlement execution (DWAC/DRS)

- Strong documentation discipline and NIGO resolution

- Stakeholder management (transfer agents, counsel, clearing firms, clients)

- Ability to prioritize and execute under strict deadlines

- Operational risk awareness and escalation judgment

- Process improvement and service mindset

Important Notes:

- Must be authorized to work full time in the U.S., BTIG does not offer sponsorship for work visas of any type

- No phone calls please, the applicant will be contacted within two weeks if successful
